## Mandate

ACTAME is developed as a joint project of two Arctic Council working groups:

- the **Protection of the Arctic Marine Environment (PAME)** working group,
  through its **Marine Protected Areas Expert Group (MPA-EG)**, and
- the **Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna (CAFF)** working group.

The project runs from 2025 to 2027 and is **led by the Norwegian Polar
Institute (NPI)**.

## Expert group and national participation

The MPA-EG brings together representatives of the Arctic States and Permanent
Participants, with observers from Arctic and international organisations. The
scoping and review of the layers assembled in ACTAME takes place through that
group, so that the tool reflects what its users — national authorities and the
working groups themselves — need it to answer.

*A list of contributing experts and their institutions will be added here.*

## Lineage

The design of ACTAME follows the CCAMLR **Weddell Sea MPA Phase 2** planning
tool, which paired an open, documented spatial data compendium with an
interactive interface so that the evidence behind a proposed MPA could be
inspected directly by everyone involved in the process. ACTAME applies that
model to the Arctic, under Arctic Council governance.
